cdec.t: Duplicate COD: fix on the server with a unique key (org, actor, client_event_id)
cdec.because: The app made a new client_event_id on every Resend. Keep the same id on resend; the server returns the earlier result instead of writing it twice.

entries.tx: The 6 trucks we lease from Tuttle Brothers Trucking have drivers on their own iPhones. Can they use the app, or do they have to switch to Android?

A lot of customers pay COD by Zelle or Venmo straight to the driver's personal account. Can the app log that, or only cash and checks?

Yes. The driver picks Transfer and takes a screenshot of the payment; accounting matches it against the bank statement when the driver turns in the end-of-shift batch. The app doesn't read bank statements itself.

src.txt: Idea, MVP and launch plan for an app that helps people find others to do something with in real life. The product's unit is a "hang" of 3–6 people with a time, a place and a set number of spots. No swiping, no DMs to strangers. Pilot neighborhood by neighborhood in Chicago.
src.ip: Every number in the blueprint is a guess and a suggested bar, not a result. The first job is to test whether people will really meet strangers around an activity.

src.txt: "Real-life meetups. Your way.": find or create activities with people nearby, from coffee, walks and concerts to workouts. Recent versions added a map, "People near you", group chat and DMs, reporting, blocking; public events only in Copenhagen. Free; English and Danish.
src.ip: Activity-first is already being done abroad, and the name Venli is very close to Venlig. Don't bring "People near you" in early: it slides into browsing profiles like a dating app.

src.t: Surgeon General's advisory on loneliness, 2023 (cited in the blueprint)
src.txt: Per the blueprint, haven't read the full advisory: about half of US adults report measurable levels of loneliness, and young adults report it the most. Social connection is linked to better health. Not specific to Chicago.
src.ip: The need to connect is real, but don't advertise with the word "lonely". People download an app to go do things, not to admit they're lonely.

src.txt: Biggest groups: Chicago Language & Culture Meetup, 7,486 members, Windy City Board Gamers, 2,637. Board game nights, book clubs, runs and language exchanges run by many groups.
src.ip: People in Chicago will already meet strangers around an activity. Meetup is great at scheduled events, weak at "tonight I want to do X".

src.txt: The BFF about page: for people who just moved to a new city or want to grow their circle, meeting people who match their "vibe". The page doesn't list which countries have the app.
src.ip: The closest big competitor talks about meeting people who match you, not about an activity with a time and a place.

src.t: Interview · Kyle, 27, just moved from Columbus for a marketing job
src.txt: 4 months in Chicago, his coworkers all have their own groups. To play board games on the weekend he posts on Reddit, waits for replies, DMs, and it takes two days to get 3 people. Last time only 1 showed up.
src.ip: The block is in filling the spots and knowing who'll really come, not in finding something to do.

src.t: Interview · Hannah, 26, works at a bank
src.txt: Wants to see movies and go to drawing workshops but doesn't want to go alone with a stranger. Tried a friend app, a few days later it was all messages asking for coffee one-on-one. Only goes if the group is 3+, in a busy place, with other women.
src.ip: Safety and not-a-date have to be built into the product flow: small groups by default, public places, women-only hangs.

src.txt: His old tennis group all got married, nobody's free. Joined 3 group chats to find pickleball partners, and every time had to ask skill level and split the $40 court fee over DMs. Got bailed on last minute twice and paid the whole court.
src.ip: Sports hangs need skill level and court fee right on the hang. Last-minute bails cost other people real money.

src.txt: Works from home all week, some days she doesn't talk to anyone. Wants to work at a café with a few people on Saturday afternoon, without much talking. Doesn't want to join a community she has to show up to regularly.
src.ip: Some hangs need quiet. A hang should say its vibe: chatty, active or focused.

src.t: Observed · r/chicago meetup threads and 2 sports group chats, 2 weeks
src.txt: Counted 214 posts looking for pickleball, tennis, running. 61% end with "DM me", no time or specific place. Only 18% had someone reply and commit to going within 24 hours.
src.ip: The need is there, but posts leave out the time, place and number of spots, so they're hard to fill. A hang template with those fields fixes exactly where it gets stuck.

src.t: App Store Review Guidelines 1.2 · user-generated content
src.txt: Per the blueprint: apps with user-generated content need a way to filter objectionable content, report it, block abusive users, and published contact info. Haven't read the latest full text to check.
src.ip: Report and block are required to ship on iPhone; signing up with a phone number also cuts fake accounts.

src.t: CPRA · precise geolocation is sensitive data (in effect since 2023)
src.txt: Per the blueprint: precise geolocation is sensitive personal information under California's CPRA, to be used only for the purpose disclosed, with a right to limit it. Haven't read the full text to check.
src.ip: Use approximate location by default; read precise location only when someone opens the map or checks in.

src.t: Concierge results · 3 weeks in Logan Square and Avondale
src.txt: 34 hangs, 118 joins, 39 different people came to at least one hang. Join → confirm 71%; confirm → show up 76%. 14 of 39 came to a second hang within 14 days. One report of a dating ask in the concierge group chat.
src.ip: Strangers will meet around something specific. Most missed hangs were before 7 AM or opened more than 3 days ahead.

src.txt: At month-end she splits the payroll file into 182 PDFs, sets each password to the person's birthday and emails them one by one. It takes most of a day. Many store staff don't have email, so she prints them and sends them to store managers. Announcements go to group texts, and a thumbs-up doesn't mean anyone read it.
src.ip: The work is in sending, reminding and answering questions, not in running payroll. The numbers are already in Excel.

src.t: Interview · 3 store managers: Silver Lake, Echo Park, Westside Mall
src.txt: Every time HR changes a schedule or a policy, the store manager texts each person and tells HR who read it. The paper time log gets photographed and texted in at the end of the day. The night shift often forgets to clock out, and the log gets fixed the next morning.
src.ip: Store managers are playing messenger between HR and staff. Read confirmations and automatic reminders take the most off their plate.

src.txt: Sent through the stores' group texts. 109 have their own smartphone, 12 share one or don't have one. 64 don't use a work email. Most want to see their pay stub on their phone.
src.ip: Don't rely on email. Account activation has to go through a phone number; a few people need a way to clock in without their own phone.

src.txt: 30 manual HR tasks, split into P0/P1/P2. Seven worth doing first: remind people who haven't answered, collect sign-ups and roll them up by team, send pay stubs from the finished file, announcements with read confirmations, fix missing hours, collect missing documents, event sign-ups.
src.ip: The list and its priorities are guesses. Use them to pick questions for interviews inside the company.

src.t: California Labor Code §226 · itemized wage statements
src.txt: With every paycheck, employers must give each employee an itemized wage statement showing gross wages, total hours worked, deductions, net pay, the pay period and every hourly rate.
src.ip: Sending pay stubs is a legal duty for Dewdrop every payday, not a nice extra.

src.txt: Employee personal information, including pay and location, is covered by the CPRA: employees get notice of what's collected and why, and it has to be used for that purpose and kept secure.
src.ip: Collect only the data we need. Ask the company's lawyer before using real payroll data.

src.txt: Plans are a monthly base fee plus a fee per person. Payroll, tax filings, time tracking, PTO, onboarding and benefits; time tracking and scheduling come with the higher plans. Annual contracts are not required.
src.ip: Buying an all-in-one HR suite means swapping out our whole HR and payroll process; Dewdrop only needs help with sending and reminding.

src.txt: Time clock, scheduling, team chat, payroll. GPS clock-in, schedules across locations, breaks and overtime alerts, time off requests and shift trades. Free for one location; paid plans priced per location.
src.ip: A multi-store time clock is something we could buy. The listing says nothing about pay stubs for staff or read confirmations for announcements.

src.txt: Unlock with Face ID or a fingerprint right on the phone; the server only gets a signature, never a face image or fingerprint.
src.ip: We can re-verify before a pay stub opens without storing any biometric data.

src.t: Timesheet measured · before and after v2

src.ip: The time clock is what stores use every day; sending and reminding is what HR needs most. Having both in one app is right.
